A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same research work and contain readable main text, equations, figures, tables, and Appendices A–T. Full-document comparison supports reliable judgments without material evidence gaps.

before.justification: v1 reports original simulated parameter-recovery experiments and analyses of macaque retinal recordings, including feature recovery for 198 cells and multi-electrode stimulation prediction for 37 cells.

after.justification: v2 retains these original simulation and retinal-recording results and additionally reports a qualitative negative result for electrical-image-only threshold prediction.

M1.justification: The HH models, inference procedures, and losses remain unchanged. The duration-feature clarification matches v1 Section 3.1 and Appendix F; the compartment-list corrections reconcile the appendices with the five-region model already described in v1 Section 4.1 and Figure 11.

E1.justification: Both versions use the same straight-axon simulations, simulated RGCs, and retinal cohorts. Electrical-image-only inference and single-electrode threshold prediction were already represented in Appendix S, so the new comparative finding in Appendix T.6 does not establish additional task coverage.

E2.justification: Appendix T.6 adds a qualitative comparison reporting failure to outperform data-driven heuristics attributed to Kato et al. (2025) and Madugula et al. (2023) on electrical-image-only threshold prediction. The comparator sets in Tables 1 and 13 remain unchanged.

E3.justification: Table 8 removes the previously listed fixed dendrite parameters from the reported simulated-RGC configuration. Table 9 corrects its metric description from mean R2 across 400 cells to R2 computed across 400 cells. These are limited corrections to reported configuration and aggregation; they do not establish that experiments were rerun.

E4.justification: The systematic feature ablations, noise-sensitivity studies, posterior-calibration analyses, amortization tests, and per-cell analyses are unchanged. Appendix T.6 adds a qualitative comparative outcome, without documenting an additional ablation, robustness study, or error breakdown.

E5.justification: Repeated-trial counts, posterior uncertainty analyses, and MLP results across 20 splits with seeds 42–61 are unchanged. The approximately 19 repeated trials newly mentioned in Table 1 were already documented in v1 Appendix O.

E6.justification: Appendix T.6 newly reports that predicting single-electrode thresholds from electrical images alone did not outperform the cited heuristics. Previously reported quantitative results remain unchanged, including 0.906 accuracy for the best HH gradient-descent model and 0.859 for the MLP in Tables 1 and 13.

T1.justification: The mathematical formulations, equations, and derivations are retained. Appendix E clarifies the relationship between capacitive–potassium and sodium–potassium duration descriptions; sodium–potassium duration was already explicitly used in v1 Appendix F. No new formal definition or proof is introduced.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction, and discussion retain the same central contributions: fitting biophysical models from extracellular measurements and predicting unseen multi-electrode responses with 90.6% accuracy. Their scientific scope is unchanged.

C2.justification: Appendix T.6 newly attributes unsuccessful electrical-image-only threshold prediction tentatively to current-shunting variation. It also removes the specific statement that arbitrary-waveform prediction requires more parameters and fewer rigid regional assumptions, although broader waveform-generalization limitations remain elsewhere.

D1.justification: v2 specifies that three additional cells provide early-stopping validation for the existing 27-training/7-test-cell MLP evaluation. It also discloses physically constrained current scale factors and clarifies cohort-specific stimulation polarities. These additions improve documentation without establishing new experimental procedures; code and data access information is unchanged.

R1.justification: v2 adds Kato et al. (2025) and Madugula et al. (2023) to the references and positions electrical-image-only threshold prediction relative to their data-driven approaches. The main related-work discussion and novelty positioning remain unchanged.

P1.justification: There are targeted explanatory rewrites concerning duration features, model regions, stimulation protocols, validation, and limitations, plus small grammatical corrections. The overall narrative and section organization are retained.

P2.justification: Table 8 loses its dendrite row, and captions for Tables 1, 9, and 13 are revised. Table 1 now distinguishes unique stimulus combinations from repeated trials using counts already given in Appendix O. Figures are unchanged, with only limited surrounding text and layout reflow.

improvement.justification: v2 improves internal consistency and reproducibility by correcting stimulus-count, compartment, and duration descriptions and identifying the MLP validation cells. The added negative comparison makes an applicability limitation clearer, although it lacks quantitative detail. Removing the specific model-expressiveness caveat slightly reduces discussion detail, but broader scope limitations remain explicit. These are useful, limited gains with unchanged headline evidence.
